usn_colorado_bb_1929.remarks_verbatim: Colorado, Maryland, West Virginia. Incomplete fourth unit Washington scrapped in 1922 as part of Washington Naval Treaty. Also known as Maryland class. Improved Tennessee design with 16 in guns. Laid down before 1925, special damage modifier of -15%. Configuration as of 1928-29 refit.
dated_remarks: 1930s: (1)8 .50 cal. added, Lt AA 0.6.
1937: SOC Seagull replaced UO-1.
1940: OS2U Kingfisher replaced Seagull.
Colorado: Jun 41 - Mar 42: in refit, fitted with torpedo bulge (Armor Rtng 29/12/135), Mk3 radar for main battery, CXAM-1 radar.
Mid-42: 5in/25 replaced by (1)8 Mk30 5in/38, 12 20mm added. Area AA 2.2, Lt AA 3.6.
Nov 42: Lt AA battery (4)4 1.1 in, 22 20mm, 8 .50 cal. mgs, Lt AA 7.4.
Nov 43: Two 5in/51, all 1.1 in, .50 cal. removed. Lt AA battery (4)6 and (2)4 40mm, 42 20mm. Lt AA 18.5.
Dec 43 - Jan 44: Brief refit at Bremerton.
Feb - May 44: Refitted at Puget Sound.
Early 44: (2)4 40mm replaced by (4)4 20mm, quad 20mm added Lt AA 20.5.
24 Jun 44: Struck by shore battery fire, minor damage.
Aug - Oct 44: Repaired at Puget Sound. Fitted with Mk8 vice Mk3 for 16in guns.
Summer 45: Planned to fit SP and SCR-720 radars, (2)8 5in/38//4 Mk12/22 with all 5in/51 and single 5in/38 removed. Area AA 4.5.
variant_notes: AF A-6 is the 1928-29 refit card. The later 1941-45 Colorado refits are transcribed in dated_remarks only; this profile is the printed card configuration.

usn_northampton_ca_1942_02.remarks_verbatim: Northampton, Chester, Louisville, Chicago, Houston, Augusta. Improved stability over Pensacola class.
dated_remarks: Mid-30s: Secondary armament upgraded to P/S(1)8 Mk11 5 in/25 and torpedo tubes removed. Area AA 0.8. Gunnery Standard IV.
1936: Torpedo tubes removed.
1940: Chester, Chicago and Northampton fitted with CXAM radar.

1941: All ships except Louisville fitted with CXAM search radar. Authorized Lt AA fit (4)4 1.1 in. Due to shortage of 1.1 in guns, some ships, including Houston, were fitted with 2P/S(1)3 Mk10 3 in/50 and (4)1 1.1 in (in place of 4th 3 inch gun). Area AA 2.5, Lt AA 0.9.
Dec 41: Houston had replaced her temporary 3in/50s with (4)4 1.1 in by this date. Total Lt AA (4)5 1.1 in, Lt AA 2.2.
Dec 41: One quad 1.1 in from Houston landed for use at Corregidor. Lt AA 1.8.
Mar 42: Houston sunk, AA fit (1) 8 Mk11 5 in, 2P/S(1)3 Mk10 3 in, (4)1 1.1. in (1) 8 .50 cal. Area AA 2.5, Lt AA 0.9.
variant_notes: AF A-14 prints the 1929 class card with Gunnery Standard III and a 4×5in/25 secondary. Houston's own Form 10 p.249 is the Feb 42 modification: GS IV, 8×5in/25, 3×3in/50. The profile follows the Form 10.
Form 10 p.249 8in/55 APC prints damage 25/19/16/14; AF C-3 prints 23/18/15/13 for the same gun row. The ship uses the Form 10 values.

usn_omaha_cl_1923.remarks_verbatim: Omaha, Milwaukee, Cincinnati, Raleigh, Detroit, Richmond, Concord, Trenton, Marblehead, Memphis. First U.S. cruiser class built since 1905. Memphis never entered combat. Laid down before 1925, special damage modifier of -15%. Search and fire control radars updated as new types became available. Gunhouses have blast protection only. Originally planned fit of two 3 inch AA doubled during construction to four. Originally fitted to lay mines, but never used after unsuccessful tests in 1924.
dated_remarks: 1935: SOC Seagull replaced UO-1.

1938-39: Cincinnati, Richmond, Concord, Trenton, and Marblehead had aft and lowest pair of 6 inch guns removed, leaving 2PW/2SW/PA/SA(1)6 Mk12 6in/53. A(1)1 6in/53 added on Marblehead. Other ships retained all 12 6 inch guns. Gunnery Standard IV.
1939-40: P/S(2)2 TT removed. Area AA fit changed to F/3P/3S/A(1)8 Mk10 3in/50, except Marblehead 3P/3S/P&S(1)7 3in/50, Area AA 2.2, Marblehead 2.0.
1940: OS2U Kingfisher replaced SOC Seagull.
Dec 41: Raleigh damaged at Pearl harbor.
Jan - Feb 42: Detroit fitted with SC-1, Mk3 radars.
Feb 42: SG, CXAM-1 radar added.
4 Feb 42: Marblehead severely damaged by air attack, arrived in New York 4 May for repairs until 15 Oct 42. Fitted with SC, SG, Mk3 radars.
Jul - Aug 42: Detroit fitted with SG radar.
Aug 42: Detroit, Raleigh, Cincinnati, and Concord fitted with (4)2 1.1 in replacing two 3in/50. Area AA 0.8, Lt AA 1.2.
Dec 42 - Jan 43: Richmond had SC replaced by SC(e), SG, Mk3 added, (4)2 1.1 in replaced by 4 40mm, Lt AA 1.6.
Feb-Mar 43: Detroit fitted with SK in place of SC, received second SC, second Mk3 radar.
Early '43: All were fitted with SC and SG (Memphis and Cincinnati had CXAM-1 instead) search radar and Mk3 for 6 in guns.
Jan 43: Richmond Lt AA (2)2 40mm replaced (4)2 1.1 inch.
Aug - Sep 43: Richmond second SG(e), second Mk3(e) radars added, Lt AA 6 40mm, 8 20mm, Lt AA 3.5.
Modified AA fit (4)2 40mm, (1)14 20mm, Lt AA 5.5.
April 1944: Milwaukee loaned to Soviet Navy. Returned to US in March 1949.
variant_notes: AF A-16 is the 1923 class card (12×6in/53, 4×3in/50, 10 torpedo tubes). The late-1930s/1942 refits (8×3in/50, torpedo tubes removed, radar) are transcribed in dated_remarks but are not the printed card configuration.
RS Form 10 p.268 is Marblehead (Omaha class, Dec 1941), a different hull with a different 6in fit; it is not used for Omaha/Memphis.

usn_clemson_4in_dd_1918.configuration: 1918 class card (AF A-19/A-20); RS Form 10 p.346 cross-check
usn_clemson_4in_dd_1918.remarks_verbatim: "Flush-deckers" or "Four-pipers." No directors, all guns use local control. Laid down before 1925, special damage modifier of -15%.
dated_remarks: Wickes class (DD 75-185) had large turning diameter, treat as B/Medium-sized ships.
Clemson class (DD 186-199, 206-7) fitted with foundations strong enough for Mk7 5in/51, but only five ships (DD 231 - 235) fitted.
DD-208 Hovey and DD-209 Long (Clemson class) had (2)4 4in/50 in twin mounts.

8 Sep 23: Seven units of Destroyer Squadron 11, all Clemson class (Chauncey, Fuller, S. P. Lee, Nicholas, Young, Delphy, Woodbury) ran aground off Honda Point and were lost. Farragut and Somers also grounded but were able to extricate themselves.
Late 30s: Early QC series sonar added.
Jan 41: Armament changed to (1)4 4in, 6 20mm (Lt AA 1.5), 6 DC Proj w/4 300 lb DC each, 2 rails w/6 Mk7 or 8 Mk6/9DC each plus 24 Mk6/9 DC. 2 sets TT removed.
1942: Assume SL radar fitted to all, those with 3 inch guns have light AA fit of (1)5 20mm vice 4 .50 cal., Lt AA 1.3.
1942-43: Remaining Wickes class to Wickes/Clemson DE (see separate entry).
May 43 on: Atlantic units (DD 109, 113, 118, 128, 142, 144, 145, 152, 220, 223, 341) fitted with HF/DF, radar to SF, one Hedgehog w/7 salvoes. One 20mm removed, Lt AA 1.0.
variant_notes: AF A-19 prints Displacement 1160/1120, Crew 114/100 and two DP rows. The profile uses the Clemson (1120 t, crew 100, DP 78) values; the Wickes variant is 1160 t, crew 114, DP 0/20/40/60/72/80.

RS Form 10 p.346 (Edsall, Clemson, Dec 1941) is a single-hull cross-check: 1090 t, crew 153, DP 0/19/39/58/69/77, Gunnery Standard II, 2×1pdr. It is not used as the class card because the AF card is the class-level annex row; the discrepancy is registered.

RS Form 10 p.346 also prints 4in/50 COM short-range damage 14 (AF C-1 prints 13) and Mk8 torpedo 75 DP (AF F-1 prints 72). The ship follows the AF C-1/F-1 annex rows; the Form 10 values are registered but not used.
AF A-19/A-20 give no radar and no 20mm for the printed 1918 fit. The 1941 refit data is in dated_remarks.

dated_remarks: Late 41: DC fit 2 Mk3 DC rail w/6 Mk7 or 8 Mk6/9 DC, 4 Mk6 K-gun w/4 Mk6/9 DC. Total of 23 Mk7 & 16 Mk6 or 41 Mk6/9 DCs carried.

rn_j_class_dd_1941_12.torpedoes_verbatim: Port & Stbd (5) 533mm TT w/5 MkIX torp
variant_notes: The only J/K/N-class Form 10 in the checked source is Jupiter (Dec 1941). It is reused as the class profile for the five catalog identities; no per-hull 1942-43 fit is invented.
The RS class index (p.13) lists Jupiter as page 33, but the actual card is PDF page 32 (page 33 is Electra). The name index (p.19) correctly says 32.

usn_gearing_dd_1944.torpedoes_verbatim: P&S(5)2 Mk14, Mk15 533mm TT w/5 Mk15 torpedoes
usn_gearing_dd_1944.remarks_verbatim: DD 710-719, 742, 743, 763-765, 782-790, 805-808, 817-853, 858-890 (only DD 710-713, 742, 743, 782-785, 805-808, 829-838, 858-860, 862-866, 873-885 commissioned during war). Lengthened Sumner class with increased fuel capacity. Stowage for 64 DCs.
dated_remarks: 1945 Anti-kamikaze modification: Aft TT mount removed. Lt AA to (4)3 40mm, (2)2 40mm, (2)9-10 20mm, Lt AA 8.5 or 9.0.

Radar Picket Conversion - DD 742, 743, 805-808, 823, 873-877 fitted with SR vice SC-2, SP radar added, TDY radar jammers, DBM (1st Gen ES), AA to (4)3 40mm (two have MK34 radars for blind-fire control), (2)2 40mm, (2)8 20mm, Lt AA 8.0. DD 742 and DD 743 had one TT mount; remainder have both mounts removed.
variant_notes: AF F-1 prints Mk15 87 DP (TNT) for the 1935-42 rows and a 1943 Torpex 99 DP row. The ship uses the registered 87 DP TNT row; the Torpex alternative is registered but not used, because the card does not date Gearing's torpedo lot.
The damage table 0/41/81/122/146/162 and speed 36/27/18/9/0 are printed at the top of A-17 and belong to the Gearing card begun on A-16.

Laid down before 1925, special damage modifier of -15%. Search and fire control radars updated as new types became available. Gunhouses have blast protection only. Originally planned fit of two 3 inch AA doubled during construction to four. Originally fitted to lay mines, but never used after unsuccessful tests in 1924.
dated_remarks: 1935: SOC Seagull replaced UO-1.

1938-39: Cincinnati, Richmond, Concord, Trenton, and Marblehead had aft and lowest pair of 6 inch guns removed, leaving 2PW/2SW/PA/SA(1)6 Mk12 6in/53. A(1)1 6in/53 added on Marblehead. Other ships retained all 12 6 inch guns. Gunnery Standard IV.
1939-40: P/S(2)2 TT removed. Area AA fit changed to F/3P/3S/A(1)8 Mk10 3in/50, except Marblehead 3P/3S/P&S(1)7 3in/50, Area AA 2.2, Marblehead 2.0.
1940: OS2U Kingfisher replaced SOC Seagull.
Dec 41: Raleigh damaged at Pearl harbor.
Jan - Feb 42: Detroit fitted with SC-1, Mk3 radars.
Feb 42: SG, CXAM-1 radar added.
4 Feb 42: Marblehead severely damaged by air attack, arrived in New York 4 May for repairs until 15 Oct 42. Fitted with SC, SG, Mk3 radars.
Jul - Aug 42: Detroit fitted with SG radar.
Aug 42: Detroit, Raleigh, Cincinnati, and Concord fitted with (4)2 1.1 in replacing two 3in/50. Area AA 0.8, Lt AA 1.2.
Dec 42 - Jan 43: Richmond had SC replaced by SC(e), SG, Mk3 added, (4)2 1.1 in replaced by 4 40mm, Lt AA 1.6.
Feb-Mar 43: Detroit fitted with SK in place of SC, received second SC, second Mk3 radar.
Early '43: All were fitted with SC and SG (Memphis and Cincinnati had CXAM-1 instead) search radar and Mk3 for 6 in guns.
Jan 43: Richmond Lt AA (2)2 40mm replaced (4)2 1.1 inch.
Aug - Sep 43: Richmond second SG(e), second Mk3(e) radars added, Lt AA 6 40mm, 8 20mm, Lt AA 3.5.
Modified AA fit (4)2 40mm, (1)14 20mm, Lt AA 5.5.
April 1944: Milwaukee loaned to Soviet Navy. Returned to US in March 1949.
